title: The World Wide recipe: A community-centred framework for fine-grained data collection and regional bias operationalisation

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing text-to-image generation accuracy, image quality, and LLM common knowledge reasoning across different geographic regions and continents, specifically contrasting historically under-resourced areas (e.g., African countries) with well-resourced areas (e.g., the US).

Evaluating representational harms, cultural flattening, and visual stereotypes in generated food images using community-centred human review, Visual Question Answering (VQA) to identify stereotypical visual elements (e.g., default dishware materials), and CLIP-based weighted cosine similarity to measure associations with positive versus negative food presentation descriptors.
